title: Replace ILP with metriko-style greedy basis-loop quantization
description:
Critical insight from /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/quantization/quantization.h: metriko (Lyon's reference impl) does NOT use a generic ILP solver. Their algorithm:

1. Construct basis-loop matrix G via sparse-QR rank reduction (rank = paper's #Vars ≈ 1.5·n_traces).
2. Initialize X = 0.
3. Greedy first-step: while validity not satisfied, pick the arc with lowest weight, find a basis loop g with g[arc] != 0, add g to X.
4. Greedy second-step: iterate sorting arcs by weight, try X±g for each basis-loop g, accept the swap that reduces Σ|X/R - 1|.
5. (Optional) Repeat with a different basis ordering (length-only sort).

This avoids ojAlgo's branch-and-bound entirely. Variable count never enters — the greedy walks the basis loops directly.

Implementation:
- Port construct_generating_vectors (basis loop construction via gen_basis_loop)
- Port reduce_to_linearly_independent (sparse QR rank reduction — Apache Commons Math has SparseQR? else Eigen-style via MTJ)
- Port the greedy two-step loop
- Use it in place of Quantization.solve when K > some threshold (or always)

Reference files:
- /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/quantization/quantization.h
- /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/quantization/quantization_basisloop.h
- /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/quantization/quantization_evaluation.h (basis loop construction)
- /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/solver/matrix_ops.h:reduce_to_linearly_independent
definition-of-done: Rocker-arm at α=15°: greedy quantization completes in <2s, produces feasible q (validates against Eq.(2)/(3)/(4)), and dmean/dmax match paper Table 1 (3.7°/14.7° within ±2°).
testing-plan: 1. Toy 4-patch fixture: greedy produces same q as direct ILP. 2. Rocker-arm at α=15°: full pipeline including Eq.(4) constraints. 3. Hand-30k: similar.
